h1:
Hat Yai Itinerary
2 Days 1 Night — Eat, Shop, Explore
intro: Two days and one night is just about the right amount of time for Hat Yai. Start the morning with dim sum, spend the late morning wandering Kim Yong Market for souvenirs, head up Khao Kho Hong in the afternoon to pay respects and catch the view, walk the night bazaar in the evening, then save Khlong Hae Floating Market for day two. This is a 2-day 1-night plan with a steady flow so you don't wear yourself out, with real spots, real timings, and a rough budget.

blocks.html: Hat Yai doesn't have a beach in the city itself, but its strengths are food and shopping, plus a handful of attractions just outside town that are easy to drive to. This plan is built for travelers who fly or take a bus in by the evening of day one, leaving a full day and a half to enjoy. It focuses on the four things people come to Hat Yai for: eating, shopping, Khao Kho Hong park, and Khlong Hae Floating Market. The one thing to plan around first: Khlong Hae Floating Market only opens Friday, Saturday and Sunday, so if you want the full plan, line up day two with one of those days.

items: Day 1 (afternoon–evening) — Check in at a central hotel, walk Kim Yong Market for souvenirs, head up Khao Kho Hong park to pay respects and watch the sunset, have dim sum or southern Thai food for dinner, and end the night at the ASEAN Night Bazaar.

Day 2 (morning–afternoon) — Start with dim sum at a well-known spot, stop by Wat Hat Yai Nai, then head to Khlong Hae Floating Market around midday for local food, pick up any souvenirs you missed, and travel home.
Where to stay — Pick a hotel around the Kim Yong Market–Lee Gardens area so you can walk to food and shopping without relying on a car all the time.
Getting around town — Short distances are walkable; for Khao Kho Hong and Khlong Hae, a taxi, Grab, or a rented motorbike is the easiest way.

blocks.title: Check before locking in your days
blocks.html: Khlong Hae Floating Market is only open Friday, Saturday and Sunday, roughly 1:00–9:00 PM. If your day two falls on a Monday–Thursday, swap Khlong Hae to the evening of day one instead, or replace it with a night market in town.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Shop Kim Yong, Climb Khao Kho Hong, Walk the Night Bazaar

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Afternoon–evening: settle in, eat, shop, take in the view

items.activity: Check in around the Kim Yong–Lee Gardens area
items.note: Staying in the city center saves you travel time the whole trip. Drop your bags and you can head straight out on foot.

items.activity: Walk Kim Yong Market for souvenirs
items.note: Open daily around 7:00 AM–6:00 PM. The afternoon is the souvenir zone — nuts, grains, dried fruit, imported snacks, dried squid. Grab the dry goods first and save the fresh stuff for the day you leave.

items.activity: Head up Khao Kho Hong, the Hat Yai municipal park
items.note: About 6 km from town, under 15 minutes by taxi or Grab. Pay respects to the white jade Guan Yin, the Brahma shrine, and the great Buddha at the summit.

items.activity: City view + sunset from the summit
items.note: The terrace around the great Buddha looks out over almost the whole city. You can ride the cable car up or drive yourself. The cable car has a closing time, so check the last run beforehand.

items.activity: Head down, back to town, dinner
items.note: Pick a dim sum spot or southern Thai restaurant in town, like Chokdee Dim Sum or one of the punchy southern places around Niphat Uthit.
On Chotwithayakul Road near the bus terminal, open around 4:00–10:00 PM. Clothes, bags, street food, plus an open-air seating area to catch the breeze. An easy way to wind down day one.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: The cable car is for the view and the photos, not the only way up the hill. If you're a group with a car, driving up is cheaper and lets you stop at every shrine at your own pace. But if you want the view from inside the gondola, it's worth one ride.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Morning Dim Sum, Temple Visit, Khlong Hae Floating Market

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Morning–afternoon: breakfast, merit-making, the floating market

items.activity: Morning dim sum at a popular spot
items.note: Hat Yai is a dim sum town. Well-known spots like Chokdee Dim Sum, Kukchai Dim Sum, or Suan Siri open early — order jim jum, har gow, shumai, steamed buns, and a pot of hot tea. This is the breakfast locals actually eat.

items.activity: Stop by Wat Hat Yai Nai for the reclining Buddha
items.note: A large reclining Buddha right in town. It doesn't take long — a good merit-making stop before you head out of the city.

items.activity: Last round of souvenirs at Kim Yong Market
items.note: Pick up fresh goods, salted fish, shrimp paste, fruit, or anything you noted yesterday. Late morning still has full stock before things sell out.

items.activity: Head to Khlong Hae Floating Market
items.note: Open Friday, Saturday and Sunday, 1:00–9:00 PM. It was the South's first floating market, about 5 km from town. Take a boat and buy food straight from the vendors' boats.

items.activity: Eat local food, stroll along the canal
items.note: Southern Thai dishes, local sweets, grilled snacks — all affordable. There's a cultural plaza with Nora dance performances at times. An easy stroll soaking up the riverside vibe.

items.activity: Travel home / head to the airport or station
items.note: If you have time left before leaving, swing by a café or grab a few more souvenirs in town. Allow about 30–45 minutes for travel.

blocks.title: If day two isn't a Friday–Sunday
blocks.html: Khlong Hae is only open those three days. If your trip doesn't line up, spend the morning finishing Kim Yong Market, then follow it with a café or some street art in town. As for the night-market vibe, move it to the evening of day one at the ASEAN Night Bazaar.

blocks.text: Food Spots and Shopping You Can Slot Into the Plan

blocks.html: These are the spots locals and travelers in Hat Yai actually go to — picked so you can slot them into the plan by taste. You don't have to hit every one; just choose what's near your route that day.

items.name: Chokdee Dim Sum
items.blurb: A legendary Hat Yai dim sum house — opens early, packed with people. Order the har gow, shumai, steamed buns, jim jum, and a pot of hot tea. Perfect for breakfast on day two.

items.name: Kukchai Dim Sum
items.blurb: Another popular dim sum spot with a wide menu and mild, easy-to-like flavors. Locals come regularly — a solid backup if Chokdee is too crowded.

items.name: Hat Yai Mina Fried Chicken (Kim Yong Market)
items.blurb: Hat Yai-style fried chicken with crispy skin and fried shallots, eaten with sticky rice. It's right inside Kim Yong Market, so you can grab a bite while you shop.

items.name: Kim Yong Market
items.blurb: The city's main souvenir source — nuts, grains, dried fruit, imported snacks, dried seafood. Open daily around 7:00 AM–6:00 PM, fresh goods in the morning, souvenirs later in the day.

items.name: ASEAN Night Bazaar
items.blurb: Night market on Chotwithayakul Road near the bus terminal — clothes, bags, street food, with an open-air seating area to catch the breeze. Open around 4:00–10:00 PM. An easy way to cap off day one.

items.name: Punchy southern Thai food around Niphat Uthit
items.blurb: Right in the city center you'll find genuine southern Thai restaurants — gaeng tai pla, stir-fried cha-om with egg, khua kling, all full-on with seasoning, eaten with fresh raw vegetables. A perfect dinner for day one.

items.name: Khao Kho Hong Park + cable car
items.blurb: Pay respects at three shrines, take in a 360-degree city view, and catch the city's best sunset spot. Drive up or ride the cable car — entry to the park is free.

items.name: Khlong Hae Floating Market
items.blurb: The South's first floating market, open Friday, Saturday and Sunday, 1:00–9:00 PM. Local food from the boats, a cultural plaza, Nora performances, and a relaxed canalside atmosphere.

blocks.html: These numbers assume two people traveling, eating reasonably well, mid-range accommodation. They cover spending within Hat Yai and don't include getting to the city (flights or coach tickets).

items: 1 night's stay (mid-range) — around ฿700–1,500 per night in the Kim Yong–Lee Gardens area.
Food for 2 days — around ฿600–1,000 per person, including dim sum, southern Thai food, and market eats.
Getting around town — taxi/Grab up the hill and out to Khlong Hae runs around ฿300–500 total, or rent a motorbike for ฿200–300 a day.
Cable car (if you ride) — around ฿100 round trip for Thai adults, about ฿50 for children.
Souvenirs — set your own budget; Kim Yong has everything from tens to hundreds of baht.

blocks.title: Keeping the budget in check
blocks.html: Food and souvenirs are the easiest things to overshoot on in Hat Yai. Set a separate souvenir budget before you walk into Kim Yong, and you'll shop happily without going overboard.

blocks.text: How to Get Around Hat Yai Smoothly

items: On foot — Kim Yong, Lee Gardens, and Niphat Uthit are all close together, easy to walk for food and shopping.
Taxi/Grab — easy to hail in town, ideal for Khao Kho Hong and Khlong Hae. Getting one back from the top of the hill can be tricky, so arrange a pickup time.
Renting a motorbike — the most flexible option if you can ride, around ฿200–300 a day, handling the hill and Khlong Hae at your own pace.
Songthaew/tuk-tuk — they run around town; always agree on the price before you get in.

faq.q: What can you do in Hat Yai in 2 days and 1 night?
faq.a: You can fit in eating, shopping, and the attractions around town. Day one focuses on walking Kim Yong Market for souvenirs, heading up Khao Kho Hong park to pay respects and take in the view, and walking the ASEAN Night Bazaar in the evening. Day two is morning dim sum, a stop at Wat Hat Yai Nai, then Khlong Hae Floating Market in the afternoon.

faq.q: What days and hours is Khlong Hae Floating Market open?
faq.a: It's open only on Friday, Saturday and Sunday, roughly 1:00–9:00 PM. It was the South's first floating market. If you want to include it in a 2-day 1-night plan, line up day two with one of those three days.

faq.q: Where should you stay in Hat Yai?
faq.a: The Kim Yong Market and Lee Gardens area is the most convenient base for food and sightseeing. You can walk to the markets, dim sum shops, and souvenirs without relying on a car much, and it's close to the ASEAN Night Bazaar too.

faq.q: Do you have to ride the cable car up Khao Kho Hong?
faq.a: No. You can easily drive or ride a motorbike up to each shrine on fully paved roads. The cable car is an option for those who want the view from inside the gondola. The fare is around ฿100 round trip for Thai adults and about ฿50 for children.

faq.q: Where's the best place to buy Hat Yai souvenirs?
faq.a: Kim Yong Market is the main souvenir source, with nuts, grains, dried fruit, imported snacks, dried squid, shrimp paste, and salted fish. It's open daily around 7:00 AM–6:00 PM, with fresh goods in the morning and souvenirs later in the day. Buy the dry goods first and save the fresh stuff for the day you leave.
